examples.solution_text:
Keep the base, use the number as the logarithm’s argument and use the index as its value.
(a) $\log_{4}64=3$
(b) $\log_{11}1=0$
(c) $\log_{6}\frac{1}{36}=-2$
(d) $\log_{125}25=\frac{2}{3}$
(e) $\log_{27}\frac{1}{3}=-\frac{1}{3}$

examples.question_text:
Write each statement in index form.
(a) $\log_{4}256=4$
(b) $\log_{13}1=0$
(c) $\log_{6}\frac{1}{216}=-3$
(d) $\log_{36}6=\frac{1}{2}$
(e) $\log_{25}\frac{1}{5}=-\frac{1}{2}$
examples.solution_text:
Raise the base to the logarithm’s value to obtain its argument.
(a) $4^{4}=256$
(b) $13^{0}=1$
(c) $6^{-3}=\frac{1}{216}$
(d) $36^{\frac{1}{2}}=6$
(e) $25^{-\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1}{5}$

The base is $13$, the index is $\frac{1}{2}$ and the argument is $\sqrt{13}$.
$13^{\frac{1}{2}}=\sqrt{13}$

examples.question_text: Write $b^{t}=N$ in logarithmic form, where $b>0$, $b\ne1$ and $N>0$.
examples.solution_text:
The base is $b$, the index is $t$ and the number is $N$.
$\log_{b}N=t$

coverage.summary: Authored four editable worked examples covering both distinct assessed conversion methods, including zero, negative, fractional, negative fractional, root and general forms. Solutions use the supplied booklet’s conversion method without logarithm laws or additional skills. Independent equations need no phantom equals gutters; diagrams are unnecessary for these symbolic conversions. Plain solution prose and mathematics inherit renderer blue. Assessments were classified only and remain unchanged; no assessment audit, file writes or visual acceptance was performed. Independent review of the new examples remains required.

examples.derivation: 4^3=64; 11^0=1; 6^-2=1/36; 125^(2/3)=5^2=25; 27^(-1/3)=1/3. Retaining each base and transferring its index to the logarithm’s value gives all five stated answers. Booklet 1 lines 138–145 and 238–250 support this conversion method and fractional variants.

Raising each logarithm base to its stated value gives 4^4=256, 13^0=1, 6^-3=1/216, 36^(1/2)=6 and 25^(-1/2)=1/5. These match every supplied argument. Booklet 1 lines 163–185 supports conversion to index form; Booklet 2 lines 527–530 explicitly supports negative fractional conversion.

The logarithm has base 13, value 1/2 and argument sqrt(13), so its equivalent index statement is 13^(1/2)=sqrt(13). The supplied identity verifies the result. Booklet 1 line 247 and lines 390–391 support root notation and its fractional-power interpretation.
By the definition of a logarithm, b^t=N is equivalent to log_b(N)=t for b>0, b≠1 and N>0. All required conditions are stated. Booklet 1 lines 108–135 supports the general conversion.

review.summary: Accepted. All 27 exact assessment locators map to the two distinct methods: index-to-log and log-to-index conversion. The four examples cover both methods and the assessed variants without introducing advanced skills. There are no existing examples to audit and no source exceptions are needed. Separate editable fields, single-dollar mathematics and plain solution prose satisfy the supplied field conventions. Independent equations need no phantom gutters; diagrams are unnecessary. Renderer blue is supported by the supplied handoff; visual capture acceptance remains a later stage. Accepted assessment mathematics was not re-audited.
